html:
Source and documentation architecture

Current behavior is defined by source, then exercising tests and configuration schemas. Current canonical guidance explains it; file/symbol contracts document ownership nearby; generated references enumerate the current structure. Historical reports remain evidence of the version and measurements they recorded.

Tier A maintained implementation requires a meaningful ownership description and significant-symbol docs. Modules may use concise native documentation; tagged contracts remain supported. Add state, lifecycle, security and compatibility details where they help a maintainer understand the implementation. Tier B operational tooling uses prose covering use, inputs, effects and cleanup. Maintained tests and validation tools also need file explanations and documentation of substantial helpers. Individual small test cases are described by their file's scenario overview. Historical source snapshots, dependencies and generated indexes retain their original contents. Production artifact and execution-cache packages remain Tier A.

The Source Module Catalog covers all maintained languages, including CSS/HTML and platform launchers. Subsystem pages expose ownership, boundaries, lifecycle, state, security and collaborators. Static imports are relationships, not a proven call graph. Compatibility/retired modules remain visible. Generated environment references publish names and owners only, never live values or secret defaults.

Use the source map to find owners, then the generated references for exhaustive paths. Before review, run .venv/bin/python scripts/source_documentation_audit.py --check. New scripts require a scope decision; new current documentation requires classification. Missing contracts and broken repository relationships fail the audit. Semantic review is still required.

Every repository folder has a README inventory, including tests, assets and historical evidence. Explain each immediate file and link child-folder guides. Use scripts/refresh_directory_guides.py --write after updating source explanations or the editorial directory-description catalog. The inventory records provenance; an extracted source summary does not constitute a completed semantic review.

The manifest-protected license README remains byte-identical. Its current inventory lives in licenses/DIRECTORY.md, checked alongside the original README hash. New license-folder guides have a separate exact-hash review; they do not change retained terms or the original notice manifest.

Python modules consumed as CLI help can use a leading ## prose block after the shebang and encoding line. Functions/classes whose docstrings feed a schema or tool description use adjacent ## comments. Both forms preserve the runtime docstring and are visible in the generated source reference.

While the annotation rollout remains incomplete, CI adds --baseline docs/engineering/source-documentation-baseline.json to reject new source documentation gaps against reviewed existing debt. This does not change the full coverage verdict. Current links and document/source classifications must still pass; the uploaded report distinguishes existing debt from new and resolved findings.

See the source standard and authority guide.

Contributor workflow

  1. Start from the source map and the relevant subsystem chapter. Read the actual registration/call site; static imports alone miss CLI, worker, platform and optional-skill entry points.
  2. For a skill, follow skill authoring: keep its definition in skills/<skill_id>/skill.py, registration in the existing catalog, and execution behind the capability adapter. Discovery and permission are separate. Keep generated capability data in package-data declarations.
  3. Characterize a changed wire or effect boundary before moving it. Preserve Pydantic class/route docstrings because frameworks consume them; put semantic ## @brief comments before declarations/decorators instead. Keep route order, public names, defaults and absent/false/zero field distinctions intact.
  4. Extend the canonical src/error_catalog/error_msg.json and existing error helpers for error identities. Credential projection belongs to src/agent_runtime/redaction.py; do not log private request envelopes.
  5. Add meaningful source contracts and update the subsystem manual. New documents need classification in docs/engineering/documentation-inventory.json and navigation in docs/document-inventory.md. Keep dated measurements historical.
  6. Run focused tests with disposable state and scripted providers. A codebase cleanup also runs the complete unit inventory before refactoring and on the final candidate, including isolated website/CMS/visual, build, evaluation, inference and native bootstrap suites. After actual documentation repairs, remove only their resolved baseline entries, retaining review evidence. Never regenerate the baseline to accept new omissions.

With the existing compatible environment, start with:

PYTHONPATH=src:tests .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_source_documentation_contract.py tests/test_documentation_links.py
.venv/bin/python scripts/source_documentation_audit.py --check --baseline docs/engineering/source-documentation-baseline.json --report-dir artifacts/code-health/docs-after
.venv/bin/python scripts/source_documentation_audit.py --prefix src/gateway_core/models.py --check
git diff --check

Select the prefix and tests for the files actually changed. The full strict audit without --baseline remains failing until old Tier-A debt is repaired; a passing regression gate does not imply full coverage. Audit output and local benchmark samples belong under ignored artifacts/. No live provider, service restart or browser campaign is necessary for source-comment edits. When executable UI or runtime code changes, exercise its actual DOM, wire, authority and recovery seams.

The offline quality tools provide the maintained Ruff commands, an exact-text guidance check and test-inventory comparison. The guidance check protects all literals conservatively. Its explicit technical-review manifest covers only the listed SQL and metadata changes; prompt resources, implemented instructions and canonical guidance fixtures remain exact. Full test reports retain existing failures, collection errors and platform skips. A rerun does not erase an earlier failure, and a partial report does not establish complete test coverage.

The October 9 cleanup report records one bounded wave, including before/after evidence and deferred extractions.
